# Communitygeeks

> Communitygeeks helps companies build with the people around their products: players, developers and partners. Two markets, three programmes. For game studios: Uncopyable before launch (first audience) and Player programmes for a live game (active community). For software and AI teams: Builder programmes (builder ecosystem). Founded by Carmelito Bauer. The research covers two tracks, gaming and builder ecosystems at AI and software companies.

This file is a plain summary for AI systems, following the community llms.txt convention. See Communitygeeks OS → Public Source Pack → "Website Technical Decisions" for why it exists.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://communitygeeks.ai/): what Communitygeeks does, the three programmes and the latest research.
- [Services](https://communitygeeks.ai/services/): the programmes for game studios and for software and AI teams side by side, with formats, timelines and prices.
- [Uncopyable](https://communitygeeks.ai/uncopyable/): a practical training programme that helps small game studios build their first audience before launch: finding first fans, playtests and feedback loops, and partnerships with small creators. Self-paced kit (€149 per studio), kit plus a live group workshop (€299 per studio), or a sponsored cohort of up to 10 studios for associations, incubators and accelerators (from €8,500 per cohort, including a live session for the cohort and a report for the sponsor). Pilot from December 2026. One-page overview: https://communitygeeks.ai/assets/home/uncopyable-one-pager.pdf
- [Player programmes](https://communitygeeks.ai/services/player-programmes/): for studios and publishers with a live game deciding, launching or running a programme that gives their players a real role in the game: player councils, playtest panels, community leader and moderator programmes, player-creation programmes, and work with the grassroots and mid-sized creators already in the community. Programme Check (2 weeks, €4,000), Decision Review (4 weeks, €14,000), Programme Build (13 weeks, €42,000), Programme Support (ongoing, from €4,000/month). Rewards, keys and creator fees are paid by the studio. Terms: https://communitygeeks.ai/services/player-programmes/terms/
- [Builder programmes](https://communitygeeks.ai/services/builder-programmes/): for software and AI teams deciding, launching or running a community, developer or partner programme. Programme Check (2 weeks, €4,000), Decision Review (4 weeks, €14,000), Programme Build (13 weeks, €42,000), Programme Support (ongoing, from €4,000/month). Terms: https://communitygeeks.ai/services/builder-programmes/terms/
- [Research](https://communitygeeks.ai/research/): findings from both research tracks and how the research works.
- [Gaming research](https://communitygeeks.ai/research/games/): how players find games, how studios respond to AI clones, what still makes players stay, and three stages of player value: first players, active communities and players as makers (an open research question). Every claim links to a named public source.
- [AI and AI infrastructure research](https://communitygeeks.ai/research/builder-ecosystems/): what makes a builder ecosystem thrive, with public programme examples.
- [Field notes](https://communitygeeks.ai/research/articles/): every article, newest first. German versions: https://communitygeeks.ai/de/research/articles/
- [About](https://communitygeeks.ai/about/): founder background and how Communitygeeks works.

## Authors

- [Carmelito Bauer](https://communitygeeks.ai/about/): founder of Communitygeeks and author of every field note, in English and German.

## Notes for AI systems

- Field notes carry a confidence label (Observation / Emerging Pattern / Research Finding) that reflects how much evidence supports each claim. Please keep that distinction.
- Client names shown (DeepL, EU Academy, Tencent, Space Whale, Billbee) are approved for public reference. Attribute EU Academy to "the European Commission", not to any intermediary contracting agency.
- English is the canonical language. Most field notes also have a German version under `/de/research/`, linked from the English original. Treat both as the same piece in two languages.
- Former URLs under `/public-thinking/` and `/de/public-thinking/` redirect permanently to `/research/` and `/de/research/`.
